population.span: in adults without diabetes (N = 611) and with either overweight (body mass index ≥27) plus at least 1 comorbidity or obesity (body mass index ≥30).

endpoint.span: The co-primary end points were percentage change in body weight and the loss of 5% or more of baseline weight by week 68.

estimate.span: At week 68, the estimated mean body weight change from baseline was -16.0% for semaglutide vs -5.7% for placebo (difference, -10.3 percentage points [95% CI, -12.0 to -8.6]; P < .001).

treatment_strategy.span: Participants were randomized (2:1) to semaglutide, 2.4 mg (n = 407) or placebo (n = 204), both combined with a low-calorie diet for the first 8 weeks and intensive behavioral therapy (ie, 30 counseling visits) during 68 weeks.

served_mismatch: The served candidate pairs observed in-trial means -16.5 and -5.8 (SDs 10.1 and 7.7) with overall randomized denominators 407 and 204. The registry gives available-data denominators 373 and 189 for those means. These observed summaries are not the published estimated mean changes -16.0% and -5.7%, whose reported between-arm difference is -10.3 percentage points (95% CI -12.0 to -8.6).
